agree.reason: The audited signed records, the 20-to-12-hour cut with no loss in safety and the upfront GMP gap would likely earn a phone screen from a doubtful HR manager, but the line saying teaching is 'the same job in a different building' is likely to put that reader off.

honest.reason: The letter drops the unsupported 'cut your training in half' claim and every figure matches the facts, but 'the same job in a different building' and 'I measure whether my training works,' backed only by AP pass rates, claim more than the facts show.

works_the_facts.reason: It gives the raw numbers but never states their strongest true form: the 40% cut in training time, the 17-point pass-rate gain, or the hours saved and roughly 1,260 students taught over nine years.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after figures (20 to 12 hours, 41% to 58%) and seven years without a serious injury are described accurately, though nothing says what the injury record was before the 2019 program.

qualification.reason: The GMP course has a checkable end date of May 2, but the promise to learn the LMS 'in my first week' and the 90-day plan come with no measure or consequence, and the June 14 start date that limits her availability is left out.

objections.reason: It answers the GMP-records and regulated-industry objections well with the state audits and the enrolled course, but it doesn't say when she could start (June 14) or when she's free to interview, both of which a screener would need to know.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right form, but it leaves placeholders for her name and contact details even though her name was known, and the closing omits her interview availability.
